I managed to inject a debug hook (__snap) into index.html that renders a single frame on demand and returns a JPEG data URL. After reloading, I called __snap with some yaw/pitch values and got back a data URL string of length ~35 KB. The tool returned that string as the value of window.__img, and I captured it in the variable.

Now I need to actually see the image. The most straightforward way would be to decode the base64 data URL locally and write it to a file, then open it. I attempted a quick PowerShell command to read a temp file, but that was just a placeholder; I haven't actually saved the base64 data yet. I also tried to POST the data back to the preview server using a fetch to '/__snap', but that endpoint doesn't exist, so the request will just fail.

What are my options? I could copy the entire base64 string from the tool output into a local file manually, but it's 35 KB and error‑prone to transcribe. I could try to pipe the string from the preview environment to the host via a custom endpoint, but that would require modifying the dev server to accept such a POST and write the payload to disk. Since I have the ability to edit files in the project, I can add a simple Express route (or similar) that listens for a POST at a known path (e.g., '/save-screenshot'), writes the body (the base64 JPEG) to a temporary file, and responds with success. That would let me send the image data directly from the preview context to the host filesystem without manual copying.

Given that I already have a temporary directory created (C:\Users\aranr\AppData\Local\Temp\wildwood) and the PowerShell command succeeded, the next logical step is to modify the dev server to accept a POST and save the screenshot. This will be more reliable than trying to reconstruct the base64 string by hand.
